headline: Houlihan Lokey cites temporary Corporate Finance headwinds
summary_short: Houlihan Lokey's fiscal Q1 2027 (calendar Q2 2026) revenue fell 15.6% y/y to $511M and net income fell to $78M ($1.15 diluted EPS, -19.0% y/y), driven by a 24% drop in Corporate Finance revenue that management called temporary rather than a cyclical downturn.
summary_long: Revenue fell 15.6% y/y to $511M as Corporate Finance revenue dropped 24% on a lower average transaction fee tied to transaction mix; FVA rose 13% on higher fee-event volume, while Financial Restructuring fell 8% on fewer closed transactions. GAAP diluted EPS fell to $1.15 (adjusted $1.35) as compensation expense fell roughly in line with revenue, but the effective tax rate rose to 9.8% from 0.5% a year ago on lower stock-based compensation deductions. Cash fell to $745M from $1,189M at fiscal year-end; operating cash flow was -$336M for the quarter, not itemized in the release. The board declared a $0.70/share dividend and repurchased 348,000 shares. Management called the headwinds temporary, not cyclical.
